name: Drizzle
description: Drizzle ORM with reviewed drizzle-kit SQL migrations on PostgreSQL, for Express, NestJS or Next.js full-stack.

specSections.title: Data Model & Migrations
specSections.guidance: For each entity/table: columns with types, lengths and numeric precision, nullability and defaults; the primary key (UUIDv7 or identity); foreign keys with an explicit on-delete behaviour; unique indexes from business rules (say which are case-insensitive); check constraints; indexes for foreign keys and query predicates; enums stored as strings; UTC timestamps; and which aggregates are edited concurrently and need a concurrency token (409 CONFLICT). Then the migration plan: one migration per change, named, in order, with which steps are expand/contract (add, backfill, switch code, drop later) so the previous version keeps working during rollout; any data backfill; the reference/seed data (dev-only seed per role and state); and how migrations run in each environment (the runtime migrator (npm run db:migrate) as the platform's pre-deploy step, or the build command gated by AIDE_RUN_MIGRATIONS on serverless hosts).

order.reason: Migrations come before the backend or Next.js server code that uses their tables.

exclusive.reason: The data engineer owns src/db and drizzle/, not endpoints, pages or services.

protectedPaths.reason: Drizzle migrations and snapshots on the base commit are immutable (FR-125); a schema change is a new migration. Only the journal is appended.

generatedFiles.ciCheck: npx drizzle-kit check && npx drizzle-kit generate && git diff --exit-code -- drizzle (no schema drift)

requiredEnv.description: PostgreSQL connection for the app (the backend, or the Next.js full-stack app when there is no backend). The Supabase transaction pooler (:6543; prepare: false with postgres.js) on serverless hosts, the session pooler (:5432) or the platform's internal URL otherwise; SSL on managed hosts.

Session pooler (:5432) used by the migrator when DATABASE_URL is the transaction pooler (serverless); the migrator falls back to DATABASE_URL when unset. Applies to the same component as DATABASE_URL.

checklist.item: Exactly one new migration per schema change, never an edit to a migration that exists on the base commit.
Breaking changes (rename, drop, type change) use expand/contract so the previous version runs against the new schema during preview and production rollout.
Columns are explicit (lengths, precision, nullability), foreign keys have a deliberate on-delete, and every foreign key and query predicate is indexed.
Uniqueness rules from the spec are unique indexes or constraints (case-insensitive where the spec says so), and concurrently edited aggregates have a concurrency token mapped to 409 CONFLICT.
Timestamps are UTC (timestamptz/datetimeoffset) from an injected clock, and enums are stored as strings.
Integration tests run against the real engine in a container with every migration applied; no in-memory or SQLite substitute.
Queries are parameterised, project only the needed columns, paginate lists and avoid N+1.
The seed is idempotent, dev-only and gated; reference data is part of the migrations.
No drizzle-kit push in package scripts or CI; npm run db:migrate (the runtime migrator) is the one-off pre-start migrate step.
Each migration has its SQL file, journal entry and snapshot, consistent with the schema (CI: drizzle-kit check and a no-drift generate).
One pool and drizzle instance with snake_case casing, injected or server-only; sql templates are parameterised.
